transcript.content: Hello, I’m Dr. AI. What brings you in today?

I'm seeking help because I've been experiencing some really extreme mood swings. For about three months, I felt unusually energetic and high, but over the last month, I've crashed into a deep state of depression. I just don't know how to cope with these shifts anymore.

During your high or low mood periods, have you ever had hallucinations or strongly believed things that others said were not true, and if so, did those experiences ever continue when your mood was otherwise normal?

No, I've never experienced any hallucinations or believed in things that others said weren't true during either my high or low periods. Even when my moods were at their most extreme, I've always felt like I had a clear grasp on reality.

During your high period, did you ever need to be hospitalized, or did the symptoms cause very serious problems like losing touch with reality, becoming dangerously impulsive, or being unable to function?

No, I've never been hospitalized, and I don't think it was quite that extreme. I was definitely overflowing with energy and doing way too much at once, but I didn't lose control or have severe problems like that.
How long did that high-energy period last, and did it last at least 4 days in a row?
Yes, it lasted for about three months straight, which is much longer than four days. I felt that high energy continuously every single day during that entire time.
Have you ever had a major depressive episode before this one that lasted at least 2 weeks and caused clear problems with work, school, or daily functioning?
I don't think I've ever had a depressive episode like this before. This past month is really the first time I've felt this deeply depressed and struggled to function.
During that three-month high period, did you have symptoms that were severe enough to make you very impaired at work, school, or in relationships, even if you were not hospitalized?

I'm not really sure, and I haven't thought much about whether it caused severe impairment back then. I was definitely doing way too much, but I don't think it caused major problems with my work or relationships.
During that high-energy period, did your mood and behavior cause clear problems that other people noticed at work, school, or in your relationships?

I'm not really sure if other people noticed or if it caused any clear problems for them. I haven't really thought about whether my behavior back then was noticeable or disruptive to the people around me.
Did that three-month high period make you very impaired in your work, school, or relationships, or was it more of an elevated but still manageable state?

It was definitely more of an elevated and manageable state rather than being severely impaired. I felt overflowing with energy and actually ended up doing far more work than I usually do. It felt like I was just highly productive rather than struggling.
Have you ever had a major depressive episode before this one that lasted at least 2 weeks and caused clear problems with work, school, or daily functioning?
I don't recall ever having a similar depressive episode before this current one. I'm really not sure, as this past month is the first time I can remember feeling this down and struggling to function.

final_diagnosis.reason: History is most consistent with a hypomanic episode lasting about 3 months (elevated energy, increased activity/productivity, no psychosis, no hospitalization, and no clear severe impairment) followed by a major depressive episode lasting at least 1 month. This pattern supports Bipolar II Disorder rather than Bipolar I Disorder, since there is no evidence of mania, psychosis, or marked functional impairment during the high period.
